                  <ns0:p>AND it came to pass after this, that David en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired of the LORD <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>Urim,</ns0:hi> as 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 23. 6, 9. and 30. 7, 8. Thus <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> begins at the right end, and lays his Foundation in Gods coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel and assistance, which now he seeks.</ns0:note>, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He asketh not whether he should take the Kingdom; for that was appointed and known before; and he would not offend God, nor disho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour his Ordinances with frivolous and unnecessary enquiries; but onely where he should enter upon it; whether in <ns0:hi>Iudab,</ns0:hi> as he supposed, because of his relation to that Tribe, and his interest in it; or whether in some other Tribe: for he doth not limit God, but resolves exactly to follow his Counsels.</ns0:note>: And the LORD said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Which was next to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> (part whereof the <ns0:hi>Iebusites</ns0:hi> now possessed) the chief City of that Tribe, and a City of the Priests: <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 21. 10, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and in the very center or middle of that Tribe, to which the whole Tribe might spee<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dily resort, when need required.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:247" />2 So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabals Wife the Carmelite.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And his men that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> with him, did David bring up, every man with his houshold: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Cities or Towns belonging and subject to <ns0:hi>He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bron,</ns0:hi> which was the <ns0:hi>Metropolis, Ios.</ns0:hi> 21. 11, 12. For in <ns0:hi>Hebron</ns0:hi> it self there was not space for them all, because it was filled with Priests, and with <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Court.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Mac. 2. 57.</ns0:note> the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This they did upon just grounds, because not onely the Kingdom was promised to that Tribe, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 49. 10. but <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> was Designed and Anointed by God, whose will both they and all <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> were obliged to observe and obey.                   <ns0:p n="5">5 ¶ And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-Gilead, and said unto them, Blessed <ns0:hi>be ye</ns0:hi> of the LORD, that <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> because.</ns0:note> ye have shewed this kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This respect and affection to procure him Burial. For as it is, and ever was esteemed an act of inhumanity to de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny Burial to the Dead; so it is an act of mercy and kindness to Bury him.</ns0:note> unto your lord, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> unto Saul, and have buried him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And now the LORD shew kindness and truth <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> True and real kindness; not in words onely, but also in actions, as you have now done to your King the Lords Anointed.</ns0:note> unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">So far am I from being offended with you for this kindness to my late Enemy, that I will requite it.</ns0:note>, because ye have done this thing.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 Therefore now let your hands be strength<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned, and † be ye valiant <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Be not afraid lest the <ns0:hi>Philistines</ns0:hi> should punish you for this Fact, but take good courage, I will defend you.</ns0:note>: for your master Saul is<ns0:note place="margin">‡ <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> be ye the Sons of valour.</ns0:note> dead <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>though your Master Saul be dead,</ns0:hi> and so your hearts may faint within you, as if you were now Sheep without a Shepherd.</ns0:note>, and also <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Know this for your com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fort that.</ns0:note> the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 ¶ But Abner the son of Ner <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Partly, out of envy and malice against <ns0:hi>David;</ns0:hi> and part<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, out of his own ambition and desire of Rule, because he knew that <ns0:hi>Ishbosheth</ns0:hi> would have onely the name of King, whilst he had the power.</ns0:note>, captain of <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">

                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And he made him king over Gilead <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Largely so taken for all the Land of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> beyond <ns0:hi>Ior<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dan,</ns0:hi> as it is <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 22. 9. <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 10. 8.</ns0:note>, and o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver the Ashurites <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Tribe of <ns0:hi>Asher,</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Chaldee</ns0:hi> Paraphrast and others understand it.</ns0:note>, and over Jezreel <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">A large and rich Valley scituate in the Borders of the Tribes of <ns0:hi>Zebulun, Issachar</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Napthali,</ns0:hi> and so put Synecdochi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cally for them all.</ns0:note>, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">the rest of.</ns0:note> Israel <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Except <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> as it follows.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Ishbosheth Sauls son <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> fourty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">To wit, before the following War broke forth. Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pare 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 13. 1. For that he Reigned longer, may appear both from the following Verse, and from <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3. 1. and from the following History. Though some think he Reigned onely two Years, and that the rest of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s seven Years the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Abner</ns0:hi>'s instigation stuck to the House of <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> but were in suspence whether they should confer the Crown upon <ns0:hi>Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phibosheth</ns0:hi> the right Heir, but a Child; or upon <ns0:hi>Ishbosheth</ns0:hi> a grown man, whom with some difficulty, and after long debates amongst themselves, they preferred.</ns0:note>: but the house of Judah followed Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 (And the <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> number of days.</ns0:note> time that David was king in He<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bron over the house of Judah, <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> seven years and six months).</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 ¶ And Abner the son of Ner, and the ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> His Officers, and Commanders, and their Army.</ns0:note> of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In the Countrey of <ns0:hi>Benjamin, Ios.</ns0:hi> 18. 25. near <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> to Fight with <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Army, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nd to bring back the rest of the King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom to <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s House.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vants of David, went out <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">To Battel. <ns0:hi>Qu.</ns0:hi> How could or durst this one Tribe op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose all the rest? <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> First, This Tribe was very number<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and valiant of themselves, and they had a King of extra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ordinary courage, and conduct, and success. Secondly, There were great numbers of the other Tribes which favoured them, as appears from 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 12. Thirdly, They had the en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />couragement of special promises of God, made both to their Tribe, and to <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and met <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> them together.</ns0:note> together <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Met the opposite Army, and put themselves into a Posture for Battel.</ns0:note> by the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 41. 12.</ns0:note> pool of Gibeon: and they sate down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And Abner said to Joab <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Abner</ns0:hi> trusting to his greater numbers, offers Battel.</ns0:note>, Let the young men now arise, and play <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Shew their prowess and dexterity in managing their Weapons, and Fighting together. He speaks like a vain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />glorious and cruel Man, and a Soldier of fortune, that e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />steemed it a sport to see Men wounding and killing one ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther. So this he designed, partly for their Mutual Recreation, and trial of Skill and Valour; and partly, that by this oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion they might be engaged in a Battel.</ns0:note> before us: and Joab said, Let them arise.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He selected all his Combatants out of that Tribe, both because that was a Warlike and Valiant Tribe; and that he might give the more honour to his own Tribe.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>pertained</ns0:hi> to Ishbo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And they caught every one his fellow by the head <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By the hair of the Head, which after their manner was of a considerable length, and therefore gave their Enemy advantage; which every one of them indeavoured to get, and to improve against the other.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>thrust</ns0:hi> his sword in his fellows side; so they fell down together: Wherefore that place was called <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is the field of strong men, <ns0:hi>or,</ns0:hi> of swords.</ns0:note> Helkath-hazzurim <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>the field of Rocks;</ns0:hi> i. e. of Men who stood like Rocks unmovable, each one dy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing upon the spot where he fought.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in Gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And there was a very sore battel that day: and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the servants of David.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 ¶ And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel <ns0:hi>was as</ns0:hi> light <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> of his feet.</ns0:note> of foot <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> as one of the Roes that is in the field.</ns0:note> as a wild Roe.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And Asahel pursued after Abner, and in go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing he turned not to the right hand, nor to the left from <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from after Abner.</ns0:note> following Abner.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Art thou Asahel? And he answered, I <ns0:hi>am.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:248" />21 And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand, or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> spoil.</ns0:note> armour <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">If thou art ambitious to get a Trophy or Mark of thy Valour, desist from me who am an old and experienced Captain, and go to some young and raw Soldier, try thy Skill upon him, and take away his Arms from him.</ns0:note>. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following of me: Wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>f</ns0:hi> He was loth to enrage <ns0:hi>Ioab</ns0:hi> too much against him, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause his guilty Conscience told him that his Cause was bad, and therefore he presaged ill success, and that he might need such a Friend as <ns0:hi>Ioab,</ns0:hi> to make his peace with <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 Howbeit, he refused to turn aside: Where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore Abner with the hinder end of the spear <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Which was sharp pointed after the manner.</ns0:note>, smote him <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 20. 10.</ns0:note> under the fifth <ns0:hi>rib</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The seat of the Liver and Bowels, where wounds are mortal.</ns0:note>, that the spear came out behind him, and he fell down there, and died in the same place <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Upon the spot, not being able to go one step further.</ns0:note>: and it came to pass, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died, stood still.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that <ns0:hi>lieth</ns0:hi> before Giah, by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 ¶ And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Where, being upon the upper ground, they might bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter defend themselves.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? Knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">It will produce dreadful effects, and many Bloody slaughters, if by a further prosecution thou makest them de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sperate; which is against all the rules of Policy.</ns0:note>? How long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turn from following their brethren <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">By Nation and Religion: whom therefore they should not pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sue with so fierce a Rage, as if they were pursuing the <ns0:hi>Phi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />listines.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 And Joab said, <ns0:hi>As</ns0:hi> God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Unless thou hadst made the motion that they might Fight, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. It was thou, not I, that gave the first occasion of this Fight. Withal, he intimates, That <ns0:hi>Almer</ns0:hi> was the sole cause of this War; and that if he had not given com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mission and command, the War had never been undertaken, but all things had been ended by an amicable agreement: which might have been made that very morning, if he had so pleased.</ns0:note>, surely then <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> from the morning.</ns0:note> in the morning, the people had <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> gone away.</ns0:note> gone up every one from following his brother.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther fought they any more <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either, First, At that time.                   <ns0:p n="29">29 And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Otherwise called, <ns0:hi>the Mountains of</ns0:hi> Bether, <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 2. 17. which were beyond <ns0:hi>Iordan.</ns0:hi> Or, some other Countrey, now not known by that name: which is the case of hundreds of places.</ns0:note>, and they came to Mahanaim.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 And Joab returned from <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of Davids servants nineteen men, and Asahel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin and of Abners men, <ns0:hi>so that</ns0:hi> three hundred and threescore men died.</ns0:p>
